en: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad: "Om"—this syllable is all this. Its further explanation is as follows: whatever has been, whatever is, and whatever will be—all that is indeed the syllable Om. And whatever else is beyond the three times, that too is indeed the syllable Om. (1)
For all this is Brahman. This Self is Brahman. This very Self has four quarters. || 2 ||
The first quarter is Vaiśvānara, whose sphere is the waking state, who perceives external objects, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who experiences gross objects. || 3 ||
The state of dreaming, internally conscious, having seven limbs and nineteen mouths, enjoying subtle objects—the Taijasa is the second quarter. || 4 ||

That state where one who is asleep desires no desire whatsoever and sees no dream—that is deep sleep (*suṣupta*). Being in the state of deep sleep, unified, a mass of consciousness alone, consisting of bliss, enjoying bliss, having the mind as its gateway—this is the wise one (*prājña*), the third quarter. || 5 ||
He is the Lord of all; He is the All-knowing; He is the Inner Controller; He is the source of all, for He is the origin and the dissolution of all beings.

It is neither inwardly cognitive, nor outwardly cognitive, nor cognitive of both; it is not a mass of consciousness, nor consciousness, nor unconsciousness. It is unseen, beyond conventional usage, ungraspable, without characteristics, unthinkable, indescribable, the essence of the realization of the one Self, the cessation of the phenomenal world, tranquil, auspicious, and non-dual. This they consider the Fourth (the *turya*). That is the Self. That is to be known. 7.
This very Self is the imperishable syllable Oṃ. With respect to its parts, it consists of measures; and the measures are the parts: the letter A, the letter U, and the letter M. || 8 ||

Vaiśvānara, whose sphere is the waking state, is the letter *a*, the first measure, because of attainment (*āpti*) or because of being the beginning (*āditva*). Indeed, he attains all desires and becomes the beginning. 9.

The Taijasa, abiding in the state of dream, is the letter *u*, the second *mātrā*, because of its excellence (*utkarṣa*) or because it stands between both. He indeed excels in the continuity of knowledge and becomes equal [to all]. In the family of one who knows this, there is no one who does not know Brahman. 10.

The state of deep sleep is the wise one (*prājña*); it is the letter *m*, the third measure. It is so called because of measuring (*mīti*) or because of non-measuring (*apīti*). Indeed, he who knows this measures all this, and he becomes the non-measurer. || 11 ||

The fourth is without measure, beyond conventional discourse, the cessation of phenomenal proliferation, auspicious, and non-dual. Thus, the syllable *oṃ* is indeed the Self. He who knows this enters the Self by means of the Self. 12.
